name: Redbox
tierWhy: The bankruptcy of its last owner, Chicken Soup for the Soul Entertainment, was converted to a Chapter 7 liquidation on July 10, 2024 and the kiosks and streaming services were shut down. The Redbox trademarks were listed for a lender’s foreclosure sale in April 2025, and we found no business renting or streaming under the name since.[^26][^32][^33]

place: DVD rental kiosks · Oakbrook Terrace, Illinois
title: Redbox (2002–2024): DVD kiosks, debt and liquidation · Spectre Brands
description: Redbox rented DVDs from about 44,000 kiosks at its 2013 peak. Rentals fell, later buyouts and sales added debt, and a judge ordered liquidation in 2024.

card.blurb: A McDonald’s side project that put a dollar-a-night video store in front of 36,000 shops. It outlived Blockbuster by a decade, changed owners four times and was switched off by a bankruptcy judge.

stat.label: kiosks switched off in July 2024, of 44,000 at the end of 2013

hero.dates: First kiosks in 2002. Liquidation ordered on Jul 10, 2024.
hero.standfirst: It beat the video store by being smaller than a parking space. Then the disc itself went out of use.
hero.deck: Redbox was a DVD rental kiosk business that began inside McDonald’s as an experiment in getting people to stop at the restaurant, and it was liquidated in 2024. Under Coinstar it grew to about 44,000 kiosks and $1.97 billion of revenue in 2013. Rentals fell every year after that. A private-equity buyout, a blank-check listing and a sale to a streaming company each added debt to a business that was shrinking, and in July 2024 a Delaware bankruptcy judge converted its owner’s case to a liquidation.

findings.title: The peak was 2013, and the owner said why.
findings.text: Rentals fell from 775.7 million in 2013 to 587.6 million in 2015. Outerwall’s annual report called it “a secular decline in the physical rental market.”[^11][^13]

findings.title: Price rises hid the fall for two years.
findings.text: The nightly DVD price went from $1.00 to $1.20 in October 2011 and to $1.50 in December 2014. Revenue per rental rose from $2.54 to $2.99 between 2013 and 2015 while the number of rentals dropped 24% (derived).[^9][^12][^13]

findings.title: Two thirds of the revenue went in two years.
findings.text: Net revenue was $858.4M in 2019, $546.2M in 2020 and $288.5M in 2021, when the pandemic cut the supply of new films.[^17]

findings.title: Every change of owner left debt on it.
findings.text: Redbox owed $325.4M at the end of 2021 and warned of substantial doubt about its future. Its next owner assumed $359.9M and was showing $970.0M of liabilities by March 2024.[^17][^22][^23]

findings.title: The machines outlasted the company.
findings.text: CVS asked the court for leave to throw out more than 2,500 kiosks. Walgreens said 5,400 were costing it $184,000 a month in electricity.[^29][^31]
